requirements.statement: Canonical text has exactly 26 ASCII characters partitioned into seven timestamp and nineteen randomness digits.
Only lowercase ASCII Base36 digits are valid; no prefixes, separators, case folding, or normalization.
Both unsigned components use exact-width lowercase Base36 encoding with leading zero padding and no truncation.
Generation uses whole-second Unix UTC timestamp in 0..36^7-1, rejecting out-of-range values.
Generation consumes exactly 12 uniformly distributed bytes from a CSPRNG; weak RNGs are forbidden.
Binary form is exactly 17 bytes: five-byte big-endian unsigned timestamp plus unchanged twelve-byte randomness; conversions are lossless.
Full validity requires exact ASCII shape and randomness <= 2^96-1; shape alone is insufficient.
Strict string/binary decoding and conversion reject malformed or out-of-range input without coercion or wrapping.
If a parser is exposed, preserve full integer timestamp and twelve randomness bytes or 24 lowercase hex characters; datetime results are UTC.
For distinct timestamps, lexicographical ordering of valid text and unsigned binary matches timestamp order; same-second order follows randomness.
A boolean full-validation API is optional; if exposed, it returns false for invalid inputs.
A format-only helper is optional; if exposed, it must not misrepresent shape-only acceptance as full validity.
If caller-supplied timestamps are supported, range-check them and still use fresh CSPRNG randomness.
Direct binary generation API is optional; if provided, it must produce a valid 17-byte identifier.
Applications should enforce uniqueness where needed and not treat identifiers as authentication secrets.
The identifier format is immutable and unversioned. No version marker, alternate alphabet, field width, or alternate binary layout may be silently substituted.
